report.verdict: Profit held (adj. EBITDA $289m, -2% YoY, in line; adj. EPS $0.10 vs $0.06 consensus) but the growth story slipped: FY26 revenue guidance was cut ~3% at the midpoint to $2.435-2.455bn on weaker U.S. multi-state jackpots, a soft Italian summer and FX, with the earlier ">5% organic growth" framing quietly re-based to roughly 2.5-3%. Ex-amortization revenue did accelerate to +4% (from ~1% in H1), but on lumpy product sales rather than wagers, leverage is now 3.30x, and nine days later the CEO announced his retirement — a lot for a 9%-yielding "pure-play lottery" thesis to digest.

summary: **Profit in line, revenue light, guidance cut.** Q3 revenue $607m (-4% reported, -3% constant currency) missed the ~$612m consensus; adj. EBITDA $289m (-2%, -1% cc) was in line with management's own expectation; adj. EPS $0.10 beat a $0.06 consensus but fell 73% YoY. GAAP income from continuing operations $45m (-53%), diluted EPS $0.12 (vs $0.29).

**Service revenue amortization (SRA) is the headline distortion — and it is growing.** Non-cash amortization of the new Italy Lotto licence fee rose to $99m from $53m (+$46m YoY). Stripping it out, revenue was $706m vs $682m, +3.5% reported / ~+4% cc — the 'operational growth' management leads with, up from ~1% in H1. FY26 incremental SRA is ~$175m and will take $0.93/share out of FY26 adj. EPS (vs $0.50 in FY25).

**Guidance bridge: revenue $2.50-2.55bn → $2.435-2.455bn (midpoint -$80m, -3.2%); adj. EBITDA $1.16-1.19bn → $1.14-1.16bn (-$25m, -2.1%).** Cash from operations is unchanged (~-$900m reported / ~+$750m ex the $1.67bn Lotto payment); capex trimmed to ~$450m (from $450-475m) on timing into 2027. Q4 EUR/USD assumption cut to 1.12 from 1.17.

**Which division drove it: U.S. & Canada (multi-state jackpots) and Italy (same-store sales plus B2C timing), then FX.** Management frames the EBITDA cut as 'primarily FX', but our arithmetic suggests FX explains only ~$15-20m of the ~$80m revenue cut (H2 euro-denominated revenue ~$600m × ~3% weaker euro) and perhaps ~$10m of the $25m EBITDA cut; the balance is jackpot and Italian volume shortfall and the deferral of some Italy B2C initiatives.

**The organic growth algorithm has been re-based without saying so.** The Q2 outlook embedded 'more than five percent organic growth' for FY26; the new outlook describes ~1% in H1, 4% in Q3 and mid-single-digit in Q4 — roughly 2.5-3% for the year on our math. The 5% medium-term CAGR 'North Star' is being re-weighted toward Italy B2C and iLottery and away from retail SSS, with a refreshed outlook promised for Q1 2027.

**Event/jackpot stats: U.S. multi-state jackpot SSS -30.6% vs +69.2% a year ago.** Q3-25 had a ~$1.8bn Powerball; Q3-26 peaked just above $1bn. MSJP wager-based revenue fell 30% to $25m. A ~$1bn Powerball was hit in New Jersey in early November, resetting the run-up against a Q4-25 comp that included another ~$1.8bn Powerball in December — hence the lower Q4 jackpot assumption. Management also conceded the Mega Millions $2→$5 redesign 'has not been all that successful' at sub-$1bn jackpot levels.

**Core demand is softer but not broken.** Global instant & draw SSS -1.0% (vs +3.9%); U.S. I&D -1.4% (vs +1.6%) yet U.S. Q3 instant sales were the second-highest Q3 in five years; Italy I&D -1.2% (vs +6.1%) on calendarization, a record heatwave (-2% retail foot traffic) and an October trucker strike; Rest of World +3.3% (vs +14.3%). Management cites a more 'intentional' lower-income consumer with strength at $20/$30/$50 price points.

**Mix did the heavy lifting: product sales $60m (+137%, +142% cc) and other service revenue $121m (+11%).** Retail terminals in Portugal, several hundred vending machines in North Carolina and higher instant-ticket printing drove product; software services (incl. Lotterywest, Western Australia) and Italy B2C drove other service. Product gross margin swung to ~25% from negative a year ago, but Q4 margin will dip as the product pipeline builds.

**Margin optics vs substance.** Reported adj. EBITDA margin 47.5% (+80bps) is inflated by SRA deflating the denominator; ex-SRA the Q3 margin was ~40.9%, down ~220bps YoY (mix, growth investment, prior-year one-time expense recoveries). YTD the ex-SRA margin is up ~40-50bps to ~41.4% (YTD adj. EBITDA +5% to $861m) — the better gauge of OPtiMa delivery.

**Cost transformation: OPtiMa target raised to $100m by 2028 (from $80m) via 'OPtiMa 3.3'.** The add-on (delayering, function consolidation, ending consulting arrangements, real-estate footprint) costs $15-20m of restructuring ($8m booked in Q2) for ~$20m annualized savings; CFO guides ~$10m incremental YoY benefit in 2027 and the final ~$20m in 2028, with an AI / business-process re-engineering program 'in the early innings'. FY26 absorbs ~$50m of growth-initiative investment.

**Below the line, leakage to minorities is large.** Of $45m income from continuing operations, $23m (51%) went to non-controlling interests (the Italy Lotto JV partners), leaving $22m attributable (-61%). Net interest expense rose $14m to $50m (lost interest income after the Lotto payment); reported ETR 36.0% (adj. 39.1%). Prior-year net income of $117m included $60m from the discontinued Gaming & Digital business.

**Cash: a weak Q3 on working capital, a solid YTD ex-Lotto.** Q3 cash from operations $73m, capex $81m, FCF -$8m. YTD CFO -$1,101m includes the $1,675m final Italy Lotto payment; ex-Lotto +$574m. YTD capex $313m (vs $239m); FCF -$1,414m. Management reiterates ~$750m FY CFO ex-Lotto, implying ~$175m in Q4.

**Balance sheet: net debt $3.84bn, leverage 3.30x (3.24x at Q2; 2.4x at Dec-25); liquidity $1.9bn ($0.5bn cash + $1.3bn undrawn).** September's €500m 4.875% senior secured notes due 2032 funded the buyback of €342m ($393m) of the 2.375% 2028s and repaid €155m ($176m) of revolver; RCF B still $463m drawn. Term-loan amortization of $227m/yr runs 2027-29.

**Capital return: $204m YTD through 9 Nov (dividends $127m + buybacks $77m), ~11% of market cap; quarterly dividend held at $0.23 (record 24 Nov, paid 8 Dec), ~9% trailing yield.** Diluted share count 185m, -5.6% YoY. Management calls repurchases at current levels 'an attractive use of capital' while insisting leverage stays within target.

**Italy regulation is a net positive with a price tag.** The draft budget law contemplates a 15-month extension of the Scratch & Win (Gratta e Vinci) concession to 31 Dec 2029 for €188m upfront, payable in two instalments (end-March and end-September 2027) with consortium partners contributing pro rata, plus a new Wednesday Lotto draw. CFO: no 'significant impact' on the leverage trajectory or the capital-return posture.

**Italy B2C build-out is real but still tiny.** MyLotteries PLAY (eInstants, eDraw, iCasino, sports betting) is being seeded via thousands of retailers; the Dual Play hybrid game delivered a record September for eInstant wagers with ~half of participants converting to the app; OTTO self-service Lotto terminals deploy from early 2027; 'Sani' proximity/payment services launched. Italy digital revenue run-rate is 'north of $10m' by year-end — immaterial for now, and 'timing' of these efforts is one of the three cited guidance drags.

**Contract pipeline: Texas and New York are the binary events.** The 10-year Texas RFP (2028-38, scored 90% technical / 10% price) has been submitted; New York executed a 2-year extension, cancelled and re-issued its RFP with a Brightstar submission due early December. Two U.S. and one international iLottery platform launches are planned over the next year; global iLottery wagers are still growing double digits.

**Management change (post-quarter, 19 Nov): CEO Vince Sadusky retires 1 Jan 2027; Thomas Warsop (CEO of ACI Worldwide 2022-26, ex-Fiserv/EDS) succeeds him.** Executive Chair Marco Sala frames it as a planned succession; Warsop has no lottery background. The Q1-27 refreshed medium-term outlook will now be a new CEO's first act — a classic reset window.

**Shares: -4.2% to $9.59 on the day (pre-market indicated -11%, intraday low $9.20), a +7% bounce on 11 Nov, then a fresh 52-week low (~$9.1) within a week; Stifel trimmed its target to $18 from $19.** At ~$1.85bn market cap and $3.84bn net debt the headline EV/FY26E adj. EBITDA is ~5x, but a large slice of that EBITDA belongs to JV minorities.

**Thesis read-through.** The defensive, cash-generative core is intact (YTD ex-SRA margin up, ex-Lotto CFO on track, dividend covered ~1.5x by ex-SRA adj. EPS), but the equity now depends on (i) jackpot luck through December, (ii) a growth algorithm migrating toward investment-heavy digital/B2C with back-ended payback, (iii) leverage staying ~3.3x through a €188m 2027 outlay and a capex step-up, and (iv) a CEO transition before the strategy refresh. The 9% yield is pricing in precisely that uncertainty.

segments.name: U.S. & Canada (49% of 9M revenue)
segments.headline: Revenue -1% to $301m as a 30.6% multi-state jackpot collapse against a $1.8bn Powerball comp swamped resilient instants; core I&D SSS -1.4% is the number to watch.
narrative: They reported U.S. & Canada revenue of $301m, down 1% both reported and in constant currency, but up 5.2% sequentially from $286m in Q2. The decline is entirely a jackpot story: total U.S. same-store sales fell 5.5% against +7.7% a year ago, split between instant & draw games at -1.4% (vs +1.6%) and multi-state jackpots at -30.6% (vs +69.2%). Q3-25 enjoyed a Powerball run to roughly $1.8bn; this year's largest run stalled just above $1bn, and multi-state jackpot wager-based revenue fell 30% to $25m. Year to date the U.S. is running at -1.6% total SSS, with I&D at -0.3% and jackpots at -13.8%. Same-store revenue, which layers contract mix onto wagers, was better than wagers at -4.6% total and +0.3% for I&D, implying ~170bps of positive contract-mix tailwind — a reminder that Brightstar's take-rate on a dollar of wagers is not static and has been drifting up as higher-rate contracts and lottery-management agreements grow.

Management's defence of the core is reasonable but selective. U.S. instant sales in Q3 were the second-highest for a third quarter in five years, behind only last year's exceptional comp, and demand for $20, $30 and $50 price points remains strong — the higher-end player is holding up while, by their own consumer research, lower-income households are the ones becoming more 'intentional' with spend amid fuel-price inflation. In the two lottery-management-agreement states where they control day-to-day operations, New Jersey and Indiana, instant sales rose 4% in the quarter and low-to-mid single digits year to date, helped by a couple of hundred additional vending machines and points of sale and more aggressive high-price-point game launches; they intend to roll this playbook across the portfolio. Stifel's question on structural cannibalization from other gambling verticals went unanswered in substance — management reverted to comps and macro — which we read as 'not yet visible in the data, but not ruled out'.

The jackpot mechanics have turned from tailwind to headwind for at least two more quarters. A ~$1bn Powerball was hit in New Jersey in the first week of November, resetting the jackpot just as the Q4-25 comparison — which included another ~$1.8bn Powerball before Christmas — gets hardest; this is the main reason the 'last 60 days' U.S. assumption was lowered. More structurally, the CEO was unusually candid that the Mega Millions redesign (ticket price $2→$5 and a new prize matrix) has produced lower play at most advertised jackpot levels, only approaching prior engagement as the jackpot nears $1bn, and he hopes the industry revisits the algorithm. With U.S. multi-state jackpots at ~4% of 9M wager-based revenue but near-100% flow-through, this is a disproportionate swing factor for EBITDA.

Product and contract activity were the quarter's U.S. bright spots. Several hundred lottery vending machines were delivered to North Carolina, contributing to the 137% jump in group product sales, and U.S. iLottery sales continued to grow strongly within a global iLottery base still compounding at double digits; two U.S. platform launches (plus one international) are slated for the next twelve months, and their Lucky Coins eInstant content is performing well in Massachusetts despite losing that platform award. On the contract front, the 10-year Texas RFP (2028-2038, scored 90% technical / 10% price) has been submitted with management 'confident', and New York signed a 2-year extension while the state cancelled and re-issued its RFP with submissions due in early December — two of the largest U.S. accounts and both binary for the 2028+ revenue base. They remain primary technology provider to 26 of 46 U.S. jurisdictions. No profit is disclosed by geography; our view is that the U.S. is the lowest-margin region (facilities-management contracts) but the one where wager-mix and LMA economics are improving.

segments.name: Italy (37% of 9M revenue)
segments.headline: Reported revenue -19% to $208m is almost entirely the $46m step-up in Lotto licence amortization; underlying wagers slipped 1.2% after +6.1% a year ago on heat, strikes and calendar.
narrative: They reported Italian revenue of $208m, down 19% reported and 18% in constant currency, and down 5.9% sequentially. The reported decline overstates reality: the $99m of upfront licence fee amortization (vs $53m) relates to the new nine-year Italy Lotto concession, whose final €1.43bn ($1.67bn) instalment was paid in April, so on our estimate Italy ex-SRA was roughly $307m vs ~$310m — about -1%, consistent with instant & draw same-store sales of -1.2% (vs +6.1%) and same-store revenue of -1.4% (vs +5.9%). Year to date Italian I&D SSS is +1.1% (vs +2.9%), which the CEO characterised as 'on top of an incredible' prior year. The quarter's EUR/USD average of 1.15 vs 1.17 cost a further ~$3m.

The explanations for the Q3 softness were plural and mostly exogenous: the calendarization effect flagged in Q2, the hottest summer on record (management cites a ~2% drop in overall retail foot traffic, not just lottery), and a trucker strike in central and southern Italy in the second half of October that delayed 'a few dozen million dollars' of instant-ticket deliveries, most of which retailers covered from in-store inventory before the government settled the dispute with tax credits. Quarter-to-date, Italy is 'roughly flat' with growth accelerating over the last week. We accept the one-off framing for the strike, less so for the heatwave — weather and consumer caution are blurring together — and note that Italy is the highest-margin geography in the group (operator economics with ~50%+ EBITDA margins on our estimate), so each point of Italian SSS matters more to EBITDA than a point in the U.S.

Regulation delivered the quarter's most consequential news, via the draft 2027 budget law rather than the results. Instead of launching the tender for the next Scratch & Win (Gratta e Vinci) concession, the draft contemplates a 15-month extension of the existing award to 31 December 2029 in exchange for €188m upfront, payable in two instalments at end-March and end-September 2027, with consortium partners contributing pro rata; it still needs parliamentary approval. The same law contemplates a new weekly Wednesday Lotto draw, which in other markets has been a sales catalyst. The CFO argued the September €500m bond, two-thirds of which retired 2028 paper, 'freed up capacity in our revolver' to fund the payment without altering the leverage trajectory or the capital-return stance — true in the short run, but it does push de-leveraging out by roughly a year on our math.

The B2C expansion — management's top growth priority — rests on three legs. First, digital gaming via the MyLotteries PLAY app (eInstants, eDraw, iCasino and sports betting), where the focus has been account activation through thousands of recruited retailers with in-store screens and the broader MyLotteries ecosystem; the Dual Play hybrid retail/digital instant game drove a record September for eInstant wagers and roughly half of participating players migrate to the app, a genuinely useful acquisition funnel. Second, OTTO, a self-service Lotto terminal creating a recurring fee-based revenue stream, deploying from early 2027. Third, 'Sani' proximity services (bill payment, phone top-ups, gift cards) leveraging the tobacconist network — a business Brightstar's predecessor once owned at scale. The honest caveat is size: Italy digital revenue is only expected to be 'north of $10m' run-rate by year-end, the 'timing of certain Italy B2C expansion efforts' is one of the three stated reasons for the revenue cut, and management acknowledges a U.S.-style investment period before profits scale, albeit with more cost control than a U.S. operator. Minority partners in the Lotto JV absorbed $23m of Q3 group net income (NCI), with $656m of partner capital contributed year to date toward the licence.

segments.name: Rest of World (14% of 9M revenue)
segments.headline: Revenue +42% to $98m on Portuguese terminal sales, Lotterywest software services and CEE contract work; the last residual drag from the UK contract exit is now behind them.
narrative: They reported Rest of World revenue of $98m, up 42% reported and 43% in constant currency, and up 27% sequentially from $77m — the fastest-growing region by a distance and now 16% of quarterly revenue versus 11% a year ago. Underlying wagers were respectable rather than spectacular: RoW instant & draw same-store sales rose 3.3% (vs a +14.3% comp), same-store revenue +1.8%, and year-to-date SSS +4.7% (vs +8.4%). The step-change came from non-wager revenue: significant retail terminal sales in Portugal (the bulk of the group's +$36m product-sales swing), software services tied to the Lotterywest contract in Western Australia, system installations in Central Europe and contract extensions in Eastern Europe, plus the iLottery platform deployed outside the U.S. The CFO put the other-service contribution at roughly +$12m in the quarter and +$30m year to date.

The UK National Lottery transition — the loss of the supplier role when the Fourth Licence changed hands — registered what management called its 'final residual impact' in Q3: about -$6m of revenue and, on our reading of the deck's bridge, about -$7m of adj. EBITDA, taking the year-to-date drag to roughly -$31m of revenue and -$32m of EBITDA (near-100% flow-through, as the cost base had already gone). From Q4 the comparison is clean, which mechanically helps reported growth into 2027.

Brazil remains a slow build. The joint venture with Scientific Games is constructing a retail network from scratch in São Paulo state and has its digital product live, alongside the long-standing Minas Gerais operation. Management's view is that the federal push against gaming under a re-elected Lula government — now before the Supreme Court — targets iCasino and sports betting, while a prior ruling confirmed states' right to run their own lotteries; they are therefore not changing course. We would treat Brazil as an option rather than a modelled contributor.

The analytical caveat is lumpiness. Portugal-scale terminal orders do not repeat on a schedule, product sales carry structurally lower margins than service revenue (the CEO explicitly guided Q4 margin lower on product mix), and management's commentary on run-rate visibility was candid that this is 'a little bit of contribution from different parts'. The recurring piece — software, maintenance and iLottery services under multi-year contracts — is the part that supports the medium-term algorithm; the hardware piece supports the quarter. With no profit disclosure by region, we assume RoW margins sit between the U.S. and Italy and rise as Lotterywest and the CEE installations move from delivery to service phase.

points: JV with Scientific Games building a retail network from scratch in São Paulo state with digital product live, alongside the long-standing Minas Gerais operation.
Federal push against gaming under a re-elected Lula government, now before the Supreme Court, targets iCasino and sports betting; a prior ruling confirmed states' right to run lotteries.
Management is not changing course.

blocks.heading: Lumpiness and margins
blocks.takeaway: The caveat is lumpiness: Portugal-scale terminal orders do not repeat on schedule and product sales carry structurally lower margins than services.
points: CEO explicitly guided Q4 margin lower on product mix.
Management candid that run-rate visibility is 'a little bit of contribution from different parts'.
Recurring software, maintenance and iLottery services under multi-year contracts support the medium-term algorithm; hardware supports the quarter.
With no regional profit disclosure, we assume RoW margins sit between the U.S. and Italy and rise as Lotterywest and CEE installations move to service phase.

quote.text: a little bit of contribution from different parts
quote.speaker: Management

highlights.text: Operational (ex-SRA, constant-currency) revenue growth accelerated to +4% from ~1% in H1, as promised on the Q2 call, and management expects the same rate in Q4; reported revenue ex-SRA was $706m vs $682m.
YTD adj. EBITDA +5% to $861m with the ex-SRA margin up ~40-50bps to ~41.4% despite ~$50m of growth investment and the UK exit — tangible evidence of OPtiMa delivery (target now $100m by 2028).

Other service revenue +11% to $121m (+$30m YTD): mostly recurring software, maintenance and iLottery services under multi-year contracts (Lotterywest, CEE extensions, Italy B2C) — the part of the mix that genuinely improves durability.

Product sales $60m (+137%) with gross margin swinging to ~25% from negative a year ago (Portugal terminals, North Carolina vending machines, instant-ticket printing) — a real profit contributor this quarter, but order-driven.

Capital return of $204m YTD through 9 Nov (~11% of market cap), dividend held at $0.23/qtr (~9% yield), share count -5.6% YoY, and buybacks continuing at a 'depressed share price' management considers attractive.

Liability management: €500m 4.875% 2032 notes issued; €342m of 2.375% 2028s and €155m of revolver repaid — the 2028 wall is largely gone and revolver headroom was rebuilt ahead of the €188m Scratch & Win payment.

Italy B2C milestones are arriving on schedule: record September eInstant wagers via Dual Play with ~50% retail-to-app conversion, OTTO terminals from early 2027, Sani proximity services launched; a possible new Wednesday Lotto draw and Scratch & Win extension to end-2029 add regulatory visibility.

lowlights.text: FY26 revenue guidance cut 3.2% at the midpoint to $2.445bn and adj. EBITDA 2.1% to $1.15bn; the prior '>5% organic growth' framing has quietly become ~1% H1 / 4% Q3 / MSD Q4 — roughly 2.5-3% for the year on our math.

U.S. multi-state jackpot SSS -30.6% (revenue -30% to $25m) against a $1.8bn Powerball comp, with another $1.8bn December comp ahead and the jackpot just reset by a ~$1bn New Jersey win; management also admits the Mega Millions $5 redesign is underperforming at sub-$1bn jackpots.

Core wagers are negative: global I&D SSS -1.0%, U.S. I&D -1.4%, Italy -1.2% (heatwave, calendar, October trucker strike). Management attributes it to comps and a cautious lower-income consumer; the cannibalization question from other gambling verticals was not directly addressed.

The EBITDA cut is attributed 'primarily to FX', yet on our arithmetic FX explains only ~$15-20m of the ~$80m revenue reduction and ~$10m of the $25m EBITDA reduction; the remainder is volume and Italy B2C timing.

Q3 ex-SRA margin fell ~220bps YoY to ~40.9% (mix toward product, growth investment, prior-year one-time expense recoveries), and Q4 margin is guided lower again on product mix; the +80bps headline margin is a denominator effect.

Leverage 3.30x (3.24x in Q2; 2.4x at Dec-25), Q3 FCF -$8m on working capital, net interest +$14m YoY, €188m due in 2027 for the Scratch & Win extension and a capex step-up into 2027 to honour the $1.6bn 2025-28 plan — de-leveraging is deferred, not cancelled.

CEO succession nine days after results: Vince Sadusky retires 1 Jan 2027, replaced by Thomas Warsop (ex-ACI Worldwide, payments/fintech, no lottery background) just before the Q1-27 strategy refresh — an obvious reset window for targets, and 51% of Q3 continuing income already leaks to JV minorities.

forecast.intro: Old vs new: FY26 revenue $2.50-2.55bn → $2.435-2.455bn (midpoint $2,525m → $2,445m, -$80m / -3.2%) and adj. EBITDA $1.16-1.19bn → $1.14-1.16bn ($1,175m → $1,150m, -$25m / -2.1%); cash from operations unchanged at ~-$900m reported / ~+$750m ex the $1.67bn Lotto payment; capex ~$450m (from $450-475m). The cut came from the U.S. & Canada (lower multi-state jackpot expectations for Q4 after the early-November Powerball hit, against a December-25 $1.8bn comp), Italy (summer heatwave and October trucker strike on same-store sales, plus deferred timing of certain B2C initiatives) and FX (Q4 EUR/USD 1.12 vs 1.17 assumed; FY 1.15). The implied Q4 is revenue $657-677m (vs $668m in Q4-25, i.e. roughly flat reported, with MSD operational growth offset by ~$30m of incremental SRA and FX) and adj. EBITDA $279-299m (vs ~$302m derived for Q4-25), a ~43% implied margin versus 47.5% in Q3 as product sales mix builds. Note that at the mid-point the full-year adj. EBITDA margin still lands ~47.0% vs 44.7% in FY25 — the headline margin expands even as ex-SRA economics are flat-to-slightly-up.

forecast.view: Our Q4-26 estimate sits at revenue ~$665m (≈flat YoY) and adj. EBITDA ~$285-290m (~43% margin), i.e. the low-to-mid part of the implied range, because the December jackpot comp is brutal and Italy is only 'roughly flat' quarter-to-date; that gives FY26E revenue ~$2.44bn and adj. EBITDA ~$1.15bn (47.0% reported, ~41% ex-SRA), with FY adj. EPS around $0.45-0.50 (estimate; includes ~$0.93 of SRA). **We expect net debt to end 2026 around $3.85-3.9bn and leverage ~3.3-3.4x**, essentially flat on Q3, then to stay ~3.3x through 2027 as the €188m Scratch & Win extension (BRSL share pro rata), higher capex and ~$170m of dividends absorb ex-Lotto free cash flow — de-leveraging resumes only if EBITDA grows. For 2027 the mechanical tailwinds are real (UK drag annualised, OPtiMa +$10m, Wednesday Lotto draw if enacted, Lotterywest and iLottery platform go-lives, product pipeline) and SRA stops rising, so reported revenue growth should turn positive; **the swing factors are jackpot luck, whether U.S. and Italian I&D wagers return to +1-2%, and the margin dilution from Italy B2C and new platforms in their investment phase.** The structural question is whether the new CEO re-bases the 5% revenue CAGR in Q1-27; our base case is a lower top-line algorithm paired with a cost/AI program, which the market has arguably already priced at a ~9% yield.
watch: December multi-state jackpot run-ups vs the Q4-25 $1.8bn Powerball comp, and any industry move to re-tune the Mega Millions matrix
Italy Q4 same-store sales after the strike (quarter-to-date 'roughly flat') and passage of the budget law: Scratch & Win extension (€188m, instalments Mar/Sep 2027) and the Wednesday Lotto draw
Texas 10-year RFP award and the New York re-issued RFP submission (early December) — the two largest U.S. contract exposures for 2028+
Q1-27 refreshed medium-term outlook under incoming CEO Thomas Warsop (from 1 Jan 2027): revenue CAGR, margin, capex envelope and the AI/BPR cost program
EUR/USD vs the 1.12 Q4 assumption (each ~1% move ≈ $2-3m quarterly revenue on our estimate) and the Q4 product-sales mix hit to margin
Leverage trajectory vs management's 'targeted range' given 3.30x today, the 2027 Scratch & Win outlay and the capex step-up; buyback pace at ~$9-10 per share
Italy B2C traction: MyLotteries PLAY account activations, OTTO terminal deployment from early 2027, Sani proximity services, and the move from a '>$10m' run-rate to something material
